text:
Recent research supports treating diagnostics as hypotheses requiring validation. [RecSys 2025’s sampling-reliability study](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) finds candidate sampling can change model rankings; [2024’s popularity-bias reproduction](https://ir.cwi.nl/pub/33989) identifies user grouping and evaluation strategy as consequential choices. [RecSys 2026’s convergent-validity study](https://md.ekstrandom.net/pubs/recsys26-eval) compares evaluation configurations against dense relevance judgments. Implication: measure sampled/full-catalog model-ranking agreement, preferably Kendall’s τ across configurations, while retaining the pinned sampled HR@10 as the selection objective. Full-catalog rankings with sparse labels are still imperfect evidence of relevance.

For this task, use fixed training-history audits, stratifying failures jointly by training-item popularity and history length; report denominators and uncertainty. Interaction counts are popularity proxies, not observed exposure probabilities: without exposure logs, do not claim exposure-normalized or causal failure rates. [Multifactorial-bias research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.18640) reinforces the limitations of correcting only one bias. The 20 qualitative users can suggest interventions but cannot establish population-level improvements or reveal unobserved conformity traits.

Recommended validation design: predeclare a diagnostic-triggered change, compare it with baseline using identical validation users and candidates, then test whether the predicted subgroup benefit accompanies higher four-category macro HR@10. Bootstrap paired per-user hit differences within each category and average the four category means equally; report the improvement and 95% interval. [Significance-testing research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.02461) supports bootstrap/randomization approaches, although its large-sample findings do not guarantee calibration with 200 users/category. These intervals measure user-sampling uncertainty, not training-seed variability or adaptive-search bias. Under the shared compute budget, prioritize a few controlled interventions; diagnostic fit alone does not establish useful model selection.
